measures: paralog margin at complete loci — an upper bound on rescue fragments, not a direct calibration of them
verdict: 24/29 contested loci of known, correctly-called identity sit below the **inherited** threshold 0.333; 3/29 sit below the threshold **in force** (0.220).

Complete loci are an upper bound on rescue fragments, so a threshold that complete evidence fails cannot be met by a fragment: under the inherited value every rescue trace would be reported `tblastn_trace_ambiguous` and no absence claim would ever be attributed. That constant does not transfer.
Observed separation at contested loci: median 0.2809, min 0.159. A threshold of 0.15 is cleared by every one of them.
D14: at all 194 loci only one family's baits aligned — the ITPR and RyR panels never contested a locus, so the family separation was decided before any margin had to be applied.
**Fragment-level, the measurement S5a deferred**: 11 rescue region(s) overlap a gene the assembly names for a paralog. The attribution agrees with that name on 11/11, over margins 0.227-0.370.
0/11 of the correct fragment attributions fall below the threshold in force (0.22); 7/11 would have fallen below the inherited 0.333 and been reported ambiguous.

No region was attributed against its annotation, so this evidence bounds the threshold from below only: it says how low the floor must be to keep correct calls, not how high it may go before wrong ones enter.
